title: Playing the red light district in long trousers and Roy Palmer
summary: As a boy he played Storyville spots with Oliver and others, wore long trousers, and recalls trombonist Roy Palmer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And then when I used to go work in the red light district. I used to go over there, he'd come and get me a little little fellow, a little kind of trouble, a friend of my union. Come at the house and tell me his dad said to go to his place at Rice's. And I put on, I had a pair of old long pants and stripes and it was heavy, big summertime, heavy piece of goods. And I put those long trousers on and go up there and play. Play with Manion and them. Manion and Francis had to wake Rice. They'd wake there a long time, long time. And a couple of times I went with King Oliver, with Joe Oliver, I mean, I worked at Pete Lada's place. I worked at Henry Zeno's place. Put on long trousers. I worked at Fue Clothes, guys, who I was drumming there. I think this boy would die, play a snare drum with John Kazmi. What's his name, Roger? Roger. Roger, I used to go to these places at Fue Clothes. Who was his band at Fue Clothes?
I loved it a kid. Whose band was at Fue Clothes?
I don't know whose band was at Fue Clothes. He probably started when he was buried here. I know Roy Palmer was working there, I remember that. I remember that good who was working there.
I think Sidney Dazmine was working there, if I can recall. It had been so long ago, I forgot.
Do you remember pianist Thomas, George W. Thomas? Do you remember ever?
Yeah, piano player? Yes. Yeah, big George. Big George Thomas, yeah, I know him, yeah.
He worked there, I think, for a while.

I think he was working there at that time, if I'm not mistaken. I think he was. I can't recall, I mean, who was working there. I remember Roy Palmer working there. That's a trombone player. Talk about getting the gutter trombone player. He was that, I don't know where he is now. But ain't nobody had no shame on Uri. That's right. Shame on Uri, Uri ain't no stuff for him. I'm gonna tell you what I feel about it, you know what I mean? Of course, you know, I hate to say those things, you know what I mean? Because guys want to be the greatest, you know what I mean? But if a man was coming to him, Roy Palmer could put you in the gutter.
